texts: On day 270 of Year 1, Meren Tallowhand told Old Vesh that the year had been difficult.
The village lost three lanterns to cold snaps in Year 1.
The village lost no lantern to the wraith beyond the six drained lanterns.
The feather store nearly ran out in the winter of Year 1.
Old Vesh told Meren Tallowhand that the sky-cat drought had caused the near-miss.
Old Vesh proposed that a few stations of the Cliff Path burn extra mire-essence in early winter in order to draw crowds of nightmoths.
Old Vesh proposed that the bright stations keep sky-cats hunting on the Cliff Path.
The Council took the proposal under consideration.

q1_issues.issue: The exceptive "beyond the six drained lanterns" is silently dropped, so the strength-0 bundle asserts the unrestricted claim that the village lost no lantern at all to the wraith — a widened denial the sentence does not make (Core patterns requires carrying the restriction or omitting the claim and recording the gap).
"The feather store nearly ran out" is parsed as an asserted run_out event at (STV 1.0 0.99), so the parse claims the store did run out, whereas the approximator cancels the eventuality.
The run_out event carries no (Past ...) atom although the clause is finite past tense, so by the status-predicate default it reads as generic/habitual.
(Degree sk_feather_store_1 run_out almost) puts a verb lemma in Degree's scale slot, which the instruction set defines as a gradable adjective or dimension noun.
The bare kind symbol sky_cat fills Agent/Theme of a specific, Ongoing/Located hunting eventuality, where the episodic bare-plural-object rule indicates a group witness rather than a kind filler.

q2_gaps: NP exceptive restricting a negated claim ("lost no lantern to the wraith BEYOND the six drained lanterns" - also 'apart from', 'other than' in this NP-exceptive use): no licensed head or scoping device; the 'other than / aside from' cues in the instruction set are only defeasible-exception cues introducing a sub-kind to a generic.

Approximator on a verbal eventuality ("nearly ran out"): the almost/nearly rule under Comparatives & degree is written only for an adjectival property (reify the state, drop the flat half, tag Degree with an adjective scale), so there is no way to record an event that nearly happened without asserting that it happened.

Mandative subjunctive complement ("proposed that a few stations burn ...", "proposed that the bright stations keep ..."): a directive-force complement is sealed as a plain declarative proposition; the instruction set has no directive-under-attitude form (Directive/Forbid is imperative-only).

Determiner "no" on an object NP ("lost no lantern"): the no/none quantifier machinery and the QuantifierPhrase companion are defined over subject ranges/kinds, so the quantifier word has no recorded carrier here.
review.notes: Strong elsewhere: past perfects inside seals keep Past with no Before, definite/named typing and compound decomposition project out of the seals while predications stay in, the six-drained-lantern group carries the descriptive modifier as a per-member rule, and the S7 seal correctly nests its own distribution rule as a sealed conjunct.

issues.reason: Core patterns states a stated restriction is never silently dropped because omitting it widens the claim, and the unrestricted strength-0 bundle denies exactly the six wraith-drained lanterns the exceptive excludes.

The approximator rule says "almost/nearly" cancels what it modifies ("the tank was almost full" asserts neither fullness nor the state), so the full-strength (Member sk_run_out_1 run_out) + (Patient ...) pair asserts an eventuality the sentence says did not occur.

Status predicates put (Past e) on finite clauses and warn never to choose between Ongoing/Past/nothing by feel; with no status atom the run_out reads as the generic/habitual default, i.e. that the feather store runs out as a matter of course.

Degree's middle slot is the stated gradable adjective (or the reserved quantity / forKind), and run_out is an event-class symbol — the same symbol this parse uses in (Member sk_run_out_1 run_out) — so the atom is ill-typed per the vocabulary.

Coordination & plurals reserves the bare kind filler for non-specific/kind-level objects and requires an existential group witness when a bare plural takes part in the occurrence, and these sky-cats are the Agent of an Ongoing, Located, Result-linked hunting eventuality.

gaps_confirmed: NP exceptive restricting a negated claim ("lost no lantern to the wraith beyond the six drained lanterns"): no exceptive head or scoping device exists; "other than / aside from" appear only as defeasible-exception cues over a generic sub-kind.

Approximator over a verbal eventuality ("nearly ran out"): the almost/nearly rule is written only for an adjectival property (reify the state, drop the flat half, tag Degree with the adjective scale), so an event that nearly happened has no licensed carrier.

Mandative subjunctive complement ("proposed that a few stations ... burn", "proposed that the bright stations keep"): the directive force is lost because sealing under Theme records a plain declarative and Directive/Forbid is defined for imperatives only.

Quantifier "no" on an object NP ("lost no lantern"): QuantifierPhrase is shaped over a subject range/kind, so the deliberate quantifier-no vs plain-not distinction the instruction set preserves for subjects collapses in object position.
new_gaps: Coreference into a prior seal: "the bright stations" re-mentions an indefinite witness minted inside the earlier proposal seal, which the instruction set says stays sealed and does not project, and the projection table licenses no route for a later clause to refer back to it.

Non-deictic season / sub-season time constants ("in the winter of Year 1", "in early winter"): the Time term vocabulary is Year/Month/Day/Weekday/Hour/Minute plus day-parts and deictic seasons (last_spring), with no bare season term that composes with a Year.

Day-of-year ordinal in a non-Gregorian calendar ("day 270 of Year 1"): (Day <n>) is the day-of-month granularity — the seeded strict ordering reads it as same-year-month day — so a day counted within a year has no licensed term.
adjudication.defect_summary: For the exceptive, no licensed form carries "beyond the six drained lanterns", so the compliant form is to leave the whole denial out and record the gap (Core patterns) rather than emit the unrestricted strength-0 bundle; for "nearly ran out" no licensed form exists either, so the compliant form is to omit the eventuality and record the gap instead of asserting (Member sk_run_out_1 run_out) — which subsumes the missing (Past sk_run_out_1), since the clause must not surface as an asserted event at all; the Degree atom has no compliant variant and should simply not be emitted (Degree's scale slot admits only a stated gradable adjective or the reserved quantity); and the sky-cats take the ordinary (GroupOf sk_group_N sky_cat) witness as the Theme of keep and the Agent of hunt.
adjudication.notes: The same episodic bare-plural-filler problem the reviewer flags at sky_cat also sits unflagged at (To sk_lose_1 cold_snap) in S2. Seal discipline is otherwise strong — definite/named typing and compound decomposition project while predications and in-P PartOf/Possession links stay sealed, and S7 nests its own distribution rule as a sealed conjunct with non-colliding variables.
